title: The Leak-Loving Lamprey
story: High above the terraced village of Sunnel, a stone aqueduct carries 480 gallons of water every hour to the fields. Marrowvex the Aqueduct Lamprey has clamped onto the channel and gulps 35% of all water that passes. Mr 6 scrambles up the arches, sword sheathed, counting instead of swinging — the farmers need to know what actually reaches them.
question: If Marrowvex swallows 35% of the 480 gallons that flow each hour, how many gallons still reach the fields each hour?
solution: The fields get the rest: 480 - 168 = 312 gallons.
So 312 gallons reach the fields each hour.
praise: Finding 35% of 480 was exactly the right first move — the last step was subtracting that gulp from the total.
hint: First work out how much the lamprey drinks (35% of 480), then ask what's left over.
victory: Mr 6 chalked the numbers right on the aqueduct wall, and Marrowvex, embarrassed to be measured so precisely, slurped off downstream to a puddle it could have all to itself. The fields drank 312 gallons that very hour.
imagePrompt: A long eel-like lamprey clamped to a sunlit stone aqueduct high above green terraced fields, while a small knightly numeral 6 in a blue cape chalks percentages on the channel wall.
